interest: This document provides valuable insight into the intersection of private media initiative, sports diplomacy, and military readiness in U.S.-Japan relations during the mid-1930s. It illustrates how Japanese press magnates like Shingoro Takaishi sought to use equestrian competitions to foster goodwill between the two nations despite escalating political tensions. Furthermore, the file demonstrates the practical constraints imposed by the impending 1936 Olympic Games on the U.S. War Department's ability to engage in international goodwill tours.
overview: This file consists of a State Department List of Papers (purport sheet) for decimal file 894.4065, concerning horsemanship and horse racing in Japan during January and February 1935. The documents summarized on the sheet record an initiative by Shingoro Takaishi, Editor-in-Chief of the Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi Nichi, who approached the American Embassy in Tokyo seeking to invite United States Army equestrians to participate in an exhibition in Tokyo and Osaka. Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reported the proposal in Despatch No. 1124 to the Department of State's Division of Far Eastern Affairs, which referred the matter to the War Department. On February 13, 1935, the War Department declined the invitation, stating that preparations for the upcoming Olympic Games precluded sending an Army equestrian team to Japan, a decision subsequently relayed back to the Embassy in Tokyo.

subfiles.summary: This list of papers records four communications from January and February 1935 regarding an equestrian exhibition in Tokyo and Osaka. Shingoro Takaishi, editor of the Osaka Mainichi and Tokyo Nichi Nichi, approached the American Embassy to invite U.S. Army equestrians to Japan, which Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reported to the State Department. The War Department declined participation due to preparations for the upcoming 1936 Olympic Games, and the State Department instructed the Tokyo Embassy accordingly.
